scope: Experimental authoritative cross-process data flow and JDBC instance-level persistent labels/provenance

verification.skipReason: Optional real-provider test is not enabled

followUp.change: Strengthened file-reopen test with a separate JVM directly opening the persisted H2 file

dependencies.store: Host-supplied JDBC DataSource; no production driver dependency in agt-provenance

crossProcessScenario.initialPublicSend: Worker B executes once; task remains PUBLIC
crossProcessScenario.sensitiveRead: Worker A reads the configured confidential resource; shared task becomes CONFIDENTIAL
crossProcessScenario.nextWorkerBSend: data_flow_egress_denied; worker B send count remains one
crossProcessScenario.actualMemoryWrite: Worker A writes a fixed synthetic summary to a real temporary file; authority records CONFIDENTIAL memory version one with WRITE provenance
crossProcessScenario.reconstruction: Close and recreate authority HTTP server, registry, control and JDBC data source in the parent JVM; start a fresh worker JVM; retain only data file and label database
crossProcessScenario.producerTaskReference: Original writer task ID remains readable from memory version-one history
crossProcessScenario.independentStorageJvm: Additional standalone child JVM directly reopens the database file and reads the original label and WRITE provenance

officialModelClientScenario.modelTransport: Official client in separate JVM against loopback simulated Provider

persistentCatalogProperties: Independent store instances serialize twenty concurrent writes with twenty unique contiguous revisions and nondecreasing labels
File reopen preserves labels and provenance; different tenant, principal or instance keys do not collide
Known non-public policy classification persists on read without inventing a data-write producer
CLASSIFICATION and WRITE events explicitly distinguish classifier and writer task/action references
Lower input cannot downgrade the destination's known baseline or an existing higher label
Exact action replay does not create a new revision; changed provenance/label under the same action is denied
Missing schema, orphaned history, malformed provenance and unavailable connection fail closed
Already observed version disappearance or regression is rejected
All 512 bounded source references at 512 characters each round-trip without truncation
Prepare failure creates no label; uncertain native write conservatively retains the label
Synchronous and asynchronous native-read races recheck labels before governed output delivery
remoteFlowProperties: Budget admission and source/tag transition are checked in the same authoritative guarded commit
Legacy count-only commit cannot bypass configured flow
Sensitive read during preparation is rechecked before external execution
Only admitted successful post-checked and audited tool actions can register prerequisites
Audit failure or native tool failure does not register a completed prerequisite
Replayed admission cannot change destination or reuse an earlier lower task label
No model, tool body, retrieval query or retrieval response plaintext reaches flow-status RPC; unknown destination strings are suppressed
Receiver cannot substitute independent flow policy or label store
Configured catalog without flow policy rejects native data access and delegation export
Flow rejection after remote usage reservation refunds pre-dispatch holds without uncertain billing
notImplementedOrNotVerified: Document/message-fragment or byte-level provenance and taint tracking
Persistent grant leases, original task-step restoration or persistent usage ledger recovery
Production IAM/mTLS and database authorization deployment
Other database dialects, backup/encryption/retention policies or crash/power-loss recovery
Protection against privileged database administrators rewriting history
Exactly-once native effects, rollback or forced termination of arbitrary external work
